blocks.content: No person who is a member of a civil service of the Union or an all-India service or a civil service of a State shall be dismissed or removed by an authority subordinate to that by which he was appointed.

rows: Tenure of office is subject to executive pleasure of President/Governor
Procedural rights and protection against arbitrary dismissal
Covers both defense personnel and civil services members
Applies strictly to civil servants of Union, State, and All-India Services
Limited by express provisions of the Constitution
Inquiry dispensable for criminal conviction, practical impossibility, or security of state

items: Article 311 protections apply exclusively to civil servants and do not extend to defense personnel or contractual employees.
Salaries and administrative expenses of major constitutional offices are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India and are non-votable.
The Doctrine of Pleasure under Article 310 is not absolute and remains subject to fundamental rights and constitutional provisions.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Civil servants hold office during the pleasure of the President or Governor as enshrined under Article 310 of the Constitution.
Article 311 provides constitutional safeguards against arbitrary dismissal, removal, or reduction in rank of civil servants.
Constitutional authorities like the CAG and UPSC members hold office for a fixed tenure of 6 years or up to 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.
Conditions of service cannot be altered to the disadvantage of constitutional post-holders after their appointment.
An inquiry under Article 311(2) can be dispensed with on grounds of national security, impracticality, or conviction on a criminal charge.
